title: Lévy distance bound for sums
statement:
There is a constant $K>0$ such that the following holds for every natural number $n$, every two probability spaces, and independent real-valued families $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ on those respective spaces. If each variable has finite third absolute moment and corresponding variables have equal means and equal second moments, then the Lévy distance between the distributions of $\sum_i X_i$ and $\sum_i Y_i$ is at most $K igl(\sum_i(\mathbb E|X_i|^3+\mathbb E|Y_i|^3) igr)^{1/4}$. Here the Lévy distance between probability measures $\mu,
u$ on $\mathbb R$ is the infimum of the numbers $\varepsilon\ge0$ such that for every $u\in\mathbb R$, $
u(( -\infty,u-\varepsilon]) -\varepsilon\le\mu(( -\infty,u])\le
u(( -\infty,u+\varepsilon]) +\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: Both underlying spaces carry probability measures
Each $X_i$ has finite third absolute moment
Each $Y_i$ has finite third absolute moment
Corresponding variables have equal second moments
